newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan agency calls for carbon dioxide cuts.
newsitem.headline: Japan agency calls for carbon dioxide cuts.

text.p: Japan's Environmental Agency on Tuesday recommended stiff action to end the nation's pollution woes, including laws to regulate greenhouse gas emissions such as carbon dioxide.
In its 1997 annual report, the government agency challenged the correctness of government policy that put industry needs ahead of the necessity to cut carbon dioxide emissions.
The report called for introduction of new taxes aimed specifically at the reduction of automobile emissions, plus new legislation aimed at more accurately pin-pointing fuel efficiency standards.

The report, which is non-binding in setting government policy, was regarded as a wake-up call to the dangers of Japan's growing auto emission levels which have given it one of the world's worst oil-guzzling images.
It also set the scene for a highly anticipated summit on global warming and the effects of carbon dioxide emissions in Japan in December.
The conference, a follow-up to the so-called Rio De Janeiro Earth summit in Brazil in 1992, represents the third meeting of the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change.
In Rio, a long list of developed nations, including Japan, made non-binding calls to reduce emissions of carbon dioxide to 1990 levels by 2000.
The Kyoto meeting will seek agreement on legally binding cuts in greenhouse gases.
